plan.english: A dark serpent lay upon the waters, and the streams did not flow. Thick darkness covered the earth. The cattle were thirsty and they grew weary. They were lying down. Then a hero, carrying a spear, went to the serpent and said to her: "Serpent, let the waters go!" She did not hear him. Then she crept toward him. He did not run away. Then he slew the serpent and split her. Then the streams burst, and they flowed. The cattle drank and were sated. The streams nourish the cattle. Great fame came to him. His fame is imperishable. Hero, you slew the serpent!

A serpent stole the brothers' cattle and hid them in a dark hollow. They sought them and did not catch sight of them. Then they came to the Grandson and said to him: "Grandson, seek our cattle!" Then he grasped a javelin and followed the path of the cattle. The path of the hooves led him to the hollow. The serpent lay in sleep and was sweating in the heat. Then she woke and became restless. Then he struck her with the javelin and slew the serpent. Then the cattle came forth from the hollow, and he drove them to the men. They gave him good fame. The Grandson's name is famous. He carried out the work successfully.

Earth the Mother was carrying a son. He is born! He is alert, and he is awake. He grew strong and drank the broth. His hands grew large. Then he stood up and seized a new javelin. She trembled. She said to him: "What do you seek?" He said: "I seek the serpent who hides the streams." Then he went to the serpent, and she caught sight of him, and she trembled in fear. Then he overcame her, and she vanished. Father Sky, your son is great!

Darkness was thick, and the cattle of Dawn lay in a hollow. The hollow was dark, and men did not catch sight of them. The cattle were thirsty and grew weary. Then Dawn, daughter of Sky, came to her brothers and said to them: "Brothers, drive my cattle from the hollow!" Then they went to the hollow and split it. Then the cattle came forth, and the hollow grew bright at dawn. Their hooves grew bright. The sun was red, and the earth became warm. The brothers milked the cattle and sacrificed to Dawn: "Dawn, giver of good things, protect us!"

The Grandson of the Waters dwells in the full river. He is Fire, and the river hides him. He burns in it. Who has seen him? Men have not seen him. Then they sought fire and went to a stream. They were saying to the stream: "Stream, give us fire!" Then it gave them the Grandson, and he warmed them, and they sweated. They cooked meat and ate it, and they were sated. They sacrificed to him. The Grandson is the giver of good things. Grandson of the Waters, give us good things!

The sun was driving swift horses, and its wheel was high. It was burning men and cattle, and the earth dried up. Then the son of Sky seized the wheel of the sun and broke it. Then the sun ran away and hid in a hollow, and darkness came. The cattle grew cold. They became slack. Men became afraid and were saying to him: "Darkness is killing us! Build a new wheel!" Then he built a new wheel and made it straight and gave it to the sun. Now it drives its wheel, and it does not burn the cattle.

The Twins drive swift horses. Their horses fly, and their chariot is swift. Dawn, daughter of Sky, is their sister. A lamb sank in a dark stream, and it said to them: "Twins, protect me! Death is swallowing me!" Then they heard its word and drove to it. Then they lifted it and seated it in the chariot. It had grown cold, and they warmed it. It rejoiced and said to the Twins: "Your fame is great. May your name be famous!"

Man and Twin dwelt in darkness. Earth was not, and sky was not. Darkness was thick. Then Man said to Twin: "Let us create the earth!" Twin said: "Brother, sacrifice me!" Then he killed him, and with his flesh he built the earth, and with his forehead he created the sky. With his heat he created the sun. Then he stood up on the earth and set up a place of sacrifice. In the place of sacrifice he placed fire. Twin became the king of death, and his name is famous. Men are the grandsons of Man.

Father Sky came to love Mother Earth. She carried daughters. The father gives water to her, and she nourishes the cattle. The cattle are productive, and men milk them. Dawn grows bright, and the sun climbs, and darkness melts. They sacrifice to Father Sky and Mother Earth. Whoever sacrifices to them, he grows rich. The father is the giver of good things. Father and Mother, protect us! May death not come to us, and may our cattle live!

Fire ran away from the place of sacrifice and hid in the waters, and the fish grew warm. They became restless and swam. Men sought him and did not find him. Then a fish said to them: "Fire lies in the river." Then they saw him. He said to the fish: "Fish, they will kill you!" Then he went to the place of sacrifice, and they sacrificed to him. Now he licks the sacrifice. Now they strike fish and cook them in the fire. Fire is the guest of men. Fire, giver of good things, do not leave us! May he burn in the place of sacrifice!

title: The Newborn God and the Cattle

plan.english: The goddess's son was born at dawn. He shod himself and went to his brother's enclosure. The brother's cattle were lying in it. Then he stole them and drove them to a hollow. He covered their path. Then the brother tracked them and came to the young one. "Young one, have you seen my cattle?" "I have not seen them, and I am young." The boy pointed out the hollow. Then the brother found them in it, and he was astonished. He came to love him. Then the boy gave him a bow, and the brother gave him the cattle. His fame is good.

A dark serpent was following the sun. Then she swallowed it, and the earth became dark. The cattle trembled in fear, and men did not plough the fields, and they did not work. Then a young hero grasped a spear and ran to the serpent. Then she caught sight of him and became afraid. Then he struck her with the spear and slew her. He slit her open, and the sun came forth from the serpent. Then it grew bright, and they rejoiced. They gave him good things. His fame is imperishable.

Dawn joined horses to the chariot and drove into the high sky. Her horses were red. Her chariot grew bright. Darkness ran away from her. Men were lying down. Then they woke and looked at her. She brought brightness to them. They are turned toward her. Then they led the cattle from the enclosure and ploughed the earth and sweated. They were saying to her: "Dawn, your horses are swift! Give us brightness and guard our cattle! May darkness not cover us!" Then she heard their words.

Warriors arrived at a full river. It was great, and its waters were swift. They became afraid and did not find a crossing. Then their king sacrificed to the river and laid a horse in it. He said: "River, goddess, giver of good things, give us a crossing!" Then it heard his word, and it stood. Then they walked on the crossing. They arrived at a field. He gave the river a bull, and it protected him.

title: The King Who Sought a Son

plan.english: A king was seeking a son. Then he sacrificed a horse and burned it in the fire. The fire licked it. Then Father Sky heard him and gave him a son. He grew up and became a great warrior. He stretched the bow. He overcame his father's enemies and drove their cattle. The father rejoiced and said to him: "Your fame is great. May you be king!" Then he became king.

The Sun's daughter was young. The Sun spoke: "Whoever wins with swift horses, he shall lead my daughter." Then men made ready chariots and horses. The Twins joined a team to a chariot. The team became restless. Then the horses ran, and their chariots broke. The Twins won, and the Sun was astonished. Then they led the Sun's daughter and seated her in the chariot. He became their father-in-law, and they became his sons-in-law. The father-in-law gives them good things. Twins, sons-in-law, guard us!

A warrior wore bronze and carried a spear and a javelin about. He went to the fight and caught sight of the enemies. They, looking at him, trembled. Then he struck an enemy and pierced him with the spear. He fell, and death seized him. His bronze was red. He was sweating. Then they ran away. He followed them and killed them. He drove their cattle and horses and gave the loot to his father. The father said to him: "Your fame will be imperishable, and your name will be famous."

A king spoke to young men: "Whoever wins, to him I shall give bronze." Then they joined horses to the chariots and drove to a stream. His son was driving swift horses. He urged them on, and they ran. They were sweating. Then his wheel broke, and he fell from the chariot. A young warrior won. He lifted his hands. Then the king gave him bronze, and he said to his son: "Your horses are swift, and you will win bronze."

A dark warrior came forth and spoke a word: "Who is a warrior?" Then a hero stood up and said to him: "I am a warrior!" Then he came near him. The dark one struck him with a javelin and did not pierce him. The javelin broke. Then he lifted a spear and struck him on the forehead. Then the dark one fell, and he took his bronze and wore it. His father rejoiced and set a famous name upon him.

A hero stood in the battle and slew enemies. A javelin flew and pierced him. He fell and said to his brother: "Death is grasping me. My fame will not vanish; fame is imperishable. Take my spear and strike them!" Then sleep covered him, and he grew cold. His hands became slack. Then they laid him on the fire, and they said: "His name will be famous."

The king spoke to the warriors: "Warriors, listen to my word! The enemies have reached our fields, and they are stealing our cattle. Seize the spears and join the horses to the chariots! Let us overcome them! Let us go to them and let us kill them! Whoever falls in the battle, his fame will be imperishable. Whoever runs away, the dogs will eat him." Then they heard the king's word and ran to them.

A father arrived from the fields, and a young man saw him. He said to him: "Young one, who is your father?" He said: "My father went to the fields of the strangers, and he is gone." "I am your father!" He did not recognize him and lifted a javelin. Then they struck with javelins. The young one's javelin broke, and the father pierced him. Then he fell, and he recognized him. He said: "Son, I killed you!" He lifted him, and he trembled. "May your fame be imperishable!"

Cattle were standing in an enclosure. A king said to young warriors: "Steal those cattle and drive them to me!" Then they went in the darkness and arrived at it. Strangers were lying down. Then they stole the cattle and drove them to him. Then those lying down woke and followed them. They stood up at a stream and slew them. They took their loot. He gave them cattle, and their fame became great.

Dawn grew bright, and a hero woke. He stood up and clothed himself in bronze. He shod himself. He grasped spear and bow and stretched the bow. Then he joined swift horses to the chariot. His brother stood in the chariot and he drove them. He said to his father: "Father, I am going to the battle. Remember me!" The father said: "May Father Sky protect you, and may you win great fame!"

A mother saw her son's horses and did not catch sight of him. She spoke to them: "Horses, what have you seen?" They said: "We have seen his death. Death seized him in the battle, and he lies in darkness." Then the mother trembled, and she said: "You were young! Death grasped you, and your fame lives. It increases. Men remember your name. May your fame be imperishable!"

title: The Stranger at the King's Table

plan.english: A stranger came to a king. He seated him and gave him meat and broth. He ate up the meat and he was sated. He was sitting in the warmth. Then he said to him: "What is your name?" He said: "My name is famous. I slew the serpent and drove the cattle from the hollow." Then he recognized him, and he rejoiced. He gave him his daughter and became his father-in-law. The father-in-law gave horses to the son-in-law.

A mother, a goddess, said to her son: "If you go to the battle, death will grasp you, and your fame will be imperishable. If you sit at your father's fire, you will see your grandsons, and your name will not be famous." Then he said: "Mother, I shall go to the battle. May death take me, and may my fame be imperishable!" Then he joined horses to a new chariot and drove to the battle. His horses flew. She kept looking at him, and she trembled. She remembers his name.

A hero fell in the battle. His horses stood and did not drink. Then they lay down. Then his twin said to them: "Swift horses, stand up! He is gone, and I will urge you on." They did not stand up. They remember him. Then Father Sky looked at them and said to them: "Horses, do not lie down! His fame is imperishable." Then they stood up and drew the chariot from the battle.

Darkness was coming, and the enemies lay in sleep. A warrior and his son-in-law grasped spears and walked in the thick darkness. They were awake. They caught sight of their horses. The horses were swift. Then he said to his son-in-law: "Lead them, and I will kill them." Then the son-in-law led them, and the warrior slew them, lying down. They did not wake. Then Dawn grew bright, and with the swift horses they arrived at their father. The father rejoiced. He gave them good things.

title: The Return of the King's Son

plan.english: A king's son dwelt among strangers. Then he went to his father's fields. His brothers did not recognize him. His dog lay in the filth. It recognized him, and death took it. Then he came to his mother. She said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am your son!" Then she recognized his speech and rejoiced. He stretched the bow. Then he slew the men who were devouring his cattle, and he became king. His fame is good.

A hero was slaying enemies in a full river, and it was red. The river spoke to him: "My waters are full! Do not slay in the river!" He did not hear it. Then it grew agitated, and it covered him. He became afraid and said to Father Sky: "Father, protect me! May I not sink!" Then Fire burned the river, and its waters boiled. Then it let him go. He went away from it.

Warriors carried a hero from the battle and laid him in a new chariot. He had grown cold. His mother sat down at the fire, and his father cut off his beard. Then they burned him with fire. The fire burned and licked him. The father spoke: "He who fell in the battle, his fame is imperishable. Let us sacrifice a horse to him, and let us remember his name!" Then they sacrificed the horse and cooked its flesh and ate it up. May his grandsons win great fame!

A thirsty wolf saw a dog. It was fat, and it was sitting. The wolf said to it: "Dog, who nourishes you?" It said: "A man nourishes me, and I guard his sheep." Then he caught sight of its enclosure and he said: "You dwell in an enclosure. I dwell in the fields. I do not seek your enclosure." Then he ran away. He was thirsty, and he lived. He who dwells in an enclosure, he is not a wolf.

A sheep standing at a stream saw horses. They were drawing a great wagon and carrying a man. The sheep said to them: "Horses, the man leads you, and you carry him. Do you not fear him?" They said: "Listen, sheep! We do not fear him. He gives us water, and he cooks your flesh." Then the sheep, hearing this, ran away into the field. He who knows man fears him.

A wolf was drinking at a full stream, and a yearling lamb was drinking. It saw the wolf and trembled in fear. Then he said to it: "Lamb, you are drinking my water!" It said: "I am not drinking it, and I am young." He said: "Your father was drinking it!" Then he seized it and ate it up. He is satisfied. The wolf does not listen to the lamb's word.

A bull was eating in a field and sweating in the heat. A locust sat down on its forehead and spoke to it: "Bull, I am great, and my wings are high. Are you not afraid of me? Shall I fly from your forehead?" The bull said: "I am not afraid of you, and I did not see you. Sit on my forehead, or fly to the field!" Then the locust flew to the field. It sat down in it. The great do not see locusts.

A dog carrying meat came to a full river. In the water it caught sight of a dog which was carrying meat. It said: "I shall seize that meat!" Then it entered the river, and its meat sank. It was swimming. It grew weary. The dog that it had caught sight of vanished. Its meat is gone, and it went away from the river. He who carries meat, let him not look at the water.

A horse dwelt by a stream, and a wolf came to him. He said to a man: "Kill the wolf!" He said: "If you carry me, I will kill it." Then he carried him, and he struck it with a spear. Then the wolf fell, and it grew cold. Then the horse said to him: "Let me go!" The man did not let him go, and he joined him to a wagon. Now the horse draws his wagon. Whoever carries a man, the man drives him.

A dog was lying in the cattle's enclosure. The cattle came from the field to the enclosure. Then it stood up and drove them from the enclosure. They said to it: "Dog, what do you eat in it?" It said: "I do not eat in it, and I lie in it." They looked at it. Then the cattle grew weary, and a man came and drove it from the enclosure. Whoever does not eat in an enclosure, let him not lie in it.

title: The Wolves, the Sheep and the Dogs

plan.english: Wolves said to sheep: "Sheep, the dogs are your enemies. Give them to us, and we will not eat you." The sheep listened to their word and gave them the dogs. Then they killed them and came to the sheep. The sheep trembled in fear and spoke to them: "Wolves, do not devour us!" They said: "The dogs are gone, and who will protect you?" Then they devoured them. They were sated. Whoever gives his dogs to the wolves, they eat him.
